subject: Liability allocation & billing-window approach — MSA + Order Form redlines
body:
From: Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinefin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Liability cap approach — initial take

Hi Mina / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Skyline is excited to move towards a pilot. Our legal has done an initial pass on the MSA and Order Form. Two quick asks on the limitation of liability:

- We need the cap to be meaningful relative to our spend. Proposing an aggregate cap equal to the greater of $500k or 12 months of fees (calculated on an annualized run rate at the time of breach).
- Prefer an annual reset (so a per-year cap) rather than a single aggregate cap across the entire term; we can discuss the multiplier for larger enterprise spend.

We also want explicit carveouts: IP infringement and willful misconduct to remain uncapped; we can live with consequential damages excluded. Please see attached Skyline_MSA_comments_20261110.docx with inline notes.

Looking for Redwood's stance so we can push through procurement.

Thanks,
Michael
Head of Legal
Skyline Financial Technologies

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Michael — appreciate the clear asks and the attached comments. High-level Redwood position to start the negotiation:

- We typically tie the primary cap to fees paid (to keep unit economics predictable). Our default is an annualized-fees approach: an annual aggregate cap equal to 1x to 2x the fees invoiced in the prior 12 months, depending on risk allocation and SLA commitments.
- We prefer annual reset (it gives both sides runway) but can consider a total term aggregate for shorter-term pilots.
- Carveouts: we can accept uncapped liability for fraud and gross negligence; we cannot accept industry-wide open-ended uncapped exposure for data breaches. For security incidents we propose a separate negotiated cap (higher multiple of fees) limited to incidents caused by Redwood's fault.

Can the legal team weigh in on whether 2x annual fees as an upper bound is acceptable, and whether a per-incident floor (e.g., $100k) plus an annual aggregate works for you. Laura / Markus / Karthik — any redline language suggestions?

Next steps: I'll coordinate a redline exchange this week and propose specific MSA text.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Michael / Mina — legal here. A few drafting points from Redwood counsel: 

1) Definition of "Fees": we recommend defining as "fees paid to Redwood under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim (excluding pass-through charges and third-party cloud bills unless Redwood invoices them)." This avoids surprise inflation of the base.

2) Structure preference: Redwood is comfortable with an annual aggregate cap set at 2x the fees paid in the prior 12 months as an upper bound for enterprise customers with SLA guarantees. For pilots or low-risk engagements we can drop to 1x.

3) Per-incident floor & aggregation: propose a per-incident cap equal to the greater of $100,000 or 0.5x monthly recurring fees (to ensure smaller customers have a meaningful per-incident remedy) with an annual aggregate cap (annual reset).

4) Carveouts: Redwood will accept uncapped liability for fraud and willful misconduct and reasonable IP indemnities. We will not accept unlimited liability for data breaches; instead propose a specific security-related cap set at 3x annual fees for incidents caused by Redwood, with an explicit carve-in for SOC2 / security controls evidence.

Please let us know if the per-incident + annual-aggregate framing is workable; we can provide precise redline language for the MSA.

Thanks,
Karthik
General Counsel (interim)
Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinefin.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Team / Michael — attaching a suggested redline of the MSA that implements the per-incident floor + annual aggregate reset approach and clarifies definitions for "Fees" and "Incident." Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_20261115.pdf (redline shows two options: Option A = 2x prior 12 months fees annual aggregate; Option B = tiered approach with per-incident and annual cap tied to ARR).

Key calls in the redline:
- Option A (preferred for enterprise): Annual aggregate cap = the greater of $500,000 or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months. Per-incident floor = $100,000.
- Option B (for larger buys): Annual aggregate cap = 2x ARR (annualized committed spend); per-incident cap = 0.5x monthly recurring fees, subject to annual aggregation.
- Security carveout language: Redwood will accept a security incident cap of 3x annual fees for incidents proven to be caused solely by Redwood. For incidents caused by joint causes or third-party cloud provider faults, liability limited to direct fees/credits (no uncapped).

I've labeled the redlines so Michael can pick preferred option and suggest edits inline.

Laura
Senior Contracts Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_20261115.pdf (redline of Sections 9-11)

---

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinefin.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Laura — redline looks good. A couple of operational clarifications before we lock language:

- Please add explicit SLA credit carveout language (credits for downtime should not count toward monetary cap). That helps preserve operational remedies without inflating liability.
- Clarify that "Fees" includes professional services when charged on the Order Form, and that any one-time implementation fees are annualized for cap calculation only if they recur.
- Recommend adding a short audit/evidence clause: Redwood will provide SOC2 report and remediation timelines; Skyline can request specific logs in good faith, subject to confidentiality and workload constraints.

I'll sign off on either Option A or Option B depending on commercial terms. Putting HubSpot deal link for reference: https://hubspot.company/deal/DEAL-8432

Markus
VP, Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinefin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Mina / team — thank you for the detailed options and redlines. Skyline is broadly comfortable with Option A (annual aggregate = greater of $500k or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months) and the per-incident floor. Two small remaining asks before procurement will greenlight: 

1) For security incidents attributable to third-party cloud provider failures (e.g., provider outage or misconfiguration that is not caused by Redwood), Skyline requests a limited higher cap of 3x annual fees for that incident year (not uncapped). Reason: our risk committee wants a discrete remedy if a cloud provider failure amplifies impact.
2) We request an explicit statement that SLA credits do not count toward the monetary cap.

If you accept those two items (which echo Markus' suggested language), we can circulate the final MSA and Order Form for signature.

Best,
Elena
Director, Procurement
Skyline Financial Technologies

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@skylinefin.com>, Michael Hastings <michael.hastings@skylinefin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Liability cap approach — initial take

Elena — thanks, appreciate the constructive framing. Redwood agrees to: 

- Accept Option A as drafted (annual aggregate = greater of $500,000 or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months).
- Add explicit SLA credit carveout (credits do not count toward the monetary cap).
- Add a narrowly tailored third-party cloud provider incident clause: where a security incident is proven to be caused solely by the cloud provider and not by Redwood, the security-related cap for that incident year will be limited to 3x annual fees (and only after Skyline has exhausted any remedies against the cloud provider). This is a firm compromise to address Skyline's risk committee ask while maintaining Redwood's exposure limits.

I'll circulate a final redline and Order Form for DocuSign once legal toggles the precise carveout language. Thanks everyone — close to final.

Mina
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
